newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian aluminium row won't affect output-Aluminiy.
newsitem.headline: Russian aluminium row won't affect output-Aluminiy.

text.p: Quarrels over foreign participation in Russia's aluminium industry should have no bearing on output and exports this year, Igor Prokopov, head of the Kontsern Aluminiy producers' group, said on Wednesday.
"I think production and exports will remain stable through all of this," he told a news conference after presenting results from the group's recent board meeting.
Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov called last month for protection of Russia's aluminium industry from western trading firms operating tolling deals with the big smelters.

David Reuben, chairman of London-based Trans-World Group, which is active in Russian tolling, slammed Kulikov's comments earlier this week in full-page letters in the The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal.

Benchmark three-month aluminium prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) rose to a 14-month high of $1,701 a tonne on Tuesday, partly on concerns that calls by Russia for curbs on foreign participation might disrupt exports to the West.
Under tolling, foreign firms bring in raw materials and pay Russian smelters to refine them, and then export the processed aluminium back to world markets.
Tolling deals account for a large chunk of Russian primary aluminium output, which last year rose to 2.87 million tonnes from 2.79 million in 1995.
Of the 1996 total, 2.44 million tonnes were exported outside the Commonwealth of Independent States.
